COLUMBUS PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH
An ACT to incorporate the Trustees Of the
Presbyterian Church in Columbus, Lowndes.

SEC. 1. Be It enacted, By The Legislature of the STATE Of Mississippi, That William W. Given, David Wright, John J. Humphrey, John Williams, Eagene B. Drake, and Robert B. Winter, be, and they are hereby created a corporation and polite, by the name Of the Trustees of the First Presbyterian Church IN Columbus, and by that name they and their successors, shall have perpetual Succession, and may receive donations, gifts, and devices, and purchase and hold real and personal estate for the use and benefit Of the said Presbyterian Church, to the amount not exceeding Fifty thousand dollars.

SEC. 2. Be It further enacted, That The said trustees shall have power to sale and convey, at their pleasure, the property which shall as aforesaid, vested in them, be capable by that name of suing and being sued, pleading and impeding in all actions and suits they may have, under seal and alter the same at pleasure, make bylaws for their own government, not inconsistent with the constitution and laws of this State, and do and perform all acts whereof corporations are capable according to the usual course Of law.

SEC. 3. Be it further enacted, That upon the death, resignation or removal from Office of the before named trustees or their successors the board of trustees shall fill such vacancies BY election from the members of said church, unless the number of trustees shall be reduced to less than three, in which case the vacancies shall be filled by the vote of the members of said church.

SEC. 4. Be it further enacted That This act shall be in full force from and after its passage.

Approved Feb. 19, 1838

The Committee on Streets and Landings have examined with all the care its great importance merits, the ordinance referred to them, entitled, "An Ordinance on Paving" and beg leave to report as follows:

But one month has elapsed since the subject was deliberately discussed, and was reported on by this committee, but only in reference the relative advantages OF the square stone and the cobblestone pavement as adapted TO the wants and the means of the people OF this municipality that question was then settled by decision OF this Council in favor OF the round stone pavement, only one Member dissenting; your committee therefore cannot believe that a repetition of the arguments then used and of the facts then stated can be necessary, nor do they deem it essential to include in the views OF the Council in order to prove the great impropriety OF investing $320,000 in wooden pavements which eighteen months ago were condemned by the unanimous vote OF this Council as pavement OF general use, and as being utterly UNsuited To our Climate, circumstances and means. A special committee then appointed, collected information from Europe and the cities of the North on the subject all OF which went to prove conclusively, that wood as material for paving street on an extensive scale had been abandoned in every city OF the United States where it had been used experimentally; and is, by the statement of the street commissioners of New York, shown TO be the most expensive and thus least durable species of pavement perhaps used. SINCE, then, your committee are aware OF no new facts favorable to wood pavement: two experiments have been made here, neither of which has stood sufficient length OF time TO furnish much information. It is known only, That the wooden pavement in St. Charles street does not answer firm and as well as was expected, and that the disagreeable flavour arising from its surface from the action of the sun after rain or damp weather, is a cause of much annoyance to the residents OF the immediate vicinity. This is ascribed to the circumstance that the surface retains impure and filthy substances thereon upon which unwholesome wastes would speedily disappear from the surface of stone pavement.

The Committee of Streets and Landings will proceed to examine the ordinance presented for their consideration; confirming themselves to the question OF the propriety of the Municipality binding itself through this Council to pave the following named streets, within and without the incorporated or taxable limits, with cubic blocks of granite at the probable of $473,000 dollars, to be made within two years: Gravier street from Circus to St. Marc street; Common from Carondelet to Claiborne; Circus from Canal to Julia street landing; Canal from Baronne to Claiborne; Poydras from Baronne to St. Marc; Perdido from Baronne to St. Marc; Camp from Delord to the upper line OF the Municipality; Carondelet from Girod to Triton Walk. Ende from Common TO the Protestant Cemetery.

It has been up to this time the fixed policy of this Council to regulate the expenditure OF the public funds by general considerations; and inasmuch as the prosperity OF commerce depends the prosperity OF our city, its first attention has been directed to the improvement of the port, by the erection OF extensive wharves throughout its whole extent, by extending and widening the quays or landings, &c. the cheap and easy transportation of produce and merchandise through our streets to and from ships and steamboats, AND the stores and warehouses OF our merchants a matter not second in importance TO the first, and consequently the paving has first been made in those streets of the greatest commercial importance: and as property is valuable IN proportion to its proximity to business so has the pavement regularly progressed from the most valuable and most frequented points, keeping pace with the wants of the community, the ability of property holders to pay their respective proportions, and the growing resources OF our treasury.

It seems to the undersigned that more just and equitable rule than this could not be devised and up to this period the whole population of this municipality have acquiesced in its propriety.
